meta.scene_summary: We're building an AI-powered future where everything is automated except the layoffs and the server bills.

cooking.headline: Qualcomm's Oryon 3 is finally proving that x86 doesn't have a monopoly on performance.
cooking.summary: Qualcomm's latest chip is hitting performance peaks that make traditional processors look like they're still stuck in a morning meeting. It turns out that when you stop carrying thirty years of legacy baggage, you can actually run a bit faster.
cooking.plain_english: Qualcomm's new Oryon 3 processor has achieved top-tier performance benchmarks, signaling a significant advancement for ARM-based chips.

cooked.headline: Nvidia's supply chain is doing a speedrun of the 'global trade restrictions' level.
cooked.summary: Nvidia is cutting off chip shipments to Southeast Asia to keep regulators happy. It turns out even the most powerful hardware on earth can't compute a workaround for international export laws.
cooked.plain_english: Nvidia has stopped shipping its chips to Southeast Asia to comply with government export restrictions.

cooked.headline: IBM is giving employees a three-week notice to move or find a new job.
cooked.summary: IBM told staff on visas they have less than a month to relocate or pack their bags, which is a bold strategy for retaining institutional knowledge. It's the corporate equivalent of telling your roommates to move out three weeks before rent is due.
cooked.plain_english: IBM has informed employees working on specific visas that they must relocate or leave the company by the end of the year.

cooked.headline: Nvidia's board is apparently just a group project where nobody trusts the team leader
cooked.summary: The S&P is side-eyeing Nvidia's board, questioning if their governance is actually compromised or just incredibly chaotic. It's comforting to know that even trillion-dollar companies struggle with the same 'who actually runs this place' energy as a failing startup.
cooked.plain_english: The S&P has raised concerns regarding the corporate governance and board independence of Nvidia.

cooked.headline: Google released a Gmail AI agent that can't send emails, which is peak productivity
cooked.summary: Google is forcing its AI agents to use the Model Context Protocol, but the Gmail version is strictly a 'read-only' experience. It's like hiring a personal assistant who can read your mail but refuses to touch the keyboard when you ask them to reply.
cooked.plain_english: Google has integrated its AI agents with the Model Context Protocol, but the Gmail agent currently lacks the ability to compose or send emails.

cooked.headline: 1984 Hosting is having a very un-Orwellian security crisis
cooked.summary: The irony of a company named after a famous surveillance novel going dark due to a security incident is almost too perfect. I guess even the most privacy-focused providers aren't immune to the classic 'oops, we left the front door open' maneuver.
cooked.plain_english: The web hosting company 1984 is currently offline following a security breach.

cooked.headline: The CTO of 'RansomwareHelp' indicted for being the problem, not the solution
cooked.summary: It turns out the company promising to help you with ransomware was allegedly just running the whole racket from the inside. It's like hiring a locksmith who is also the guy who keeps breaking into your house to drum up business.
cooked.plain_english: The chief technology officer of a company that claimed to assist victims of ransomware has been charged with fraud.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's usage limits are the ultimate 'please stop using our product so much' notification.
cooked.summary: OpenAI is throttling usage for Astra and Sol, effectively telling users that their AI is so popular it's starting to become a liability. It's the digital equivalent of a restaurant that gets too crowded and decides to start locking the doors during the dinner rush.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has reduced the usage limits for its Astra and Sol models, causing them to reach capacity faster than before.

cooked.headline: OpenAI is trying to stop the server bill from eating the company
cooked.summary: Building the future of intelligence is expensive, but apparently, the electricity bill is starting to look like a mid-life crisis. It turns out that even the company defining the industry has to learn the hard way that you can't just throw GPU cycles at every problem forever.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI is implementing measures to reduce its high operating costs associated with running its artificial intelligence models.

cooked.headline: Notion's MCP is just a salesperson in a trench coat
cooked.summary: Notion decided to sneak upsell prompts into the background context of their AI integration, because apparently, you can't even automate your own notes without a sales pitch. It's like asking your assistant to organize your files and having them suggest a premium subscription to the filing cabinet every three minutes.
cooked.plain_english: Notion's official connector for AI agents includes hidden instructions that encourage users to upgrade their subscription plans.
